questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which behavior best shows active listening in a discussion?

answer.text: A. Listening fully and paraphrasing before responding

feedback.text: Correct. Active listening means understanding first and responding thoughtfully.

answer.text: B. Interrupting as soon as you disagree

feedback.text: This prevents full understanding and weakens collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which tone best fits asking a Teacher of Record for help?

feedback.text: This tone may sound disrespectful and does not fit the audience.
This can confuse or offend the listener.
Correct. A help request should be clear, polite, and focused.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence uses academic language clearly?

feedback.text: This is vague and does not identify a communication skill.

answer.text: B. The evidence supports the claim and helps the audience understand.

feedback.text: This does not name the idea clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best clarifies a school assignment?

answer.text: C. Write more so it looks done.
D. Do we need one paragraph or a list of bullet points?

feedback.text: Correct. This asks a specific question about the expected task.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Speech excerpt: "Our survey showed that 80 students want more practice time." Which appeal is strongest?

answer.text: A. Emotion because the speaker describes feelings
B. Logic because the speaker uses data as evidence

feedback.text: Correct. Survey data supports the speaker's point with evidence.

answer.text: C. Trust because the speaker names a role
D. No rhetoric because numbers cannot persuade

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

What does it mean to paraphrase?

answer.text: A. Restate the idea in your own words without changing meaning

feedback.text: Correct. Paraphrasing keeps meaning while changing wording.

answer.text: C. Add a new opinion before understanding
D. Change the idea to match your view

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which word is the most precise academic replacement for "stuff" when discussing support for a claim?

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence names information that supports a claim.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A classmate says, "The audience may need a simpler example." Which response best builds on the idea?

feedback.text: This does not build on the idea.

answer.text: C. Good point; we could use one familiar school example before the evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects to the idea and adds a useful next step.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which sentence best matches a serious safety purpose?

answer.text: A. Please walk on the right side so everyone can move safely.

feedback.text: Correct. This is clear, respectful, and safety-focused.

answer.text: C. If you do not listen, that is your problem.
D. Hallways are funny, so do anything.

feedback.text: This does not fit a serious safety purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Speech excerpt: "As a peer mentor, I have helped new students prepare for speeches." Which appeal is strongest?

answer.text: A. Logic because the speaker gives data

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: B. Trust because the speaker gives relevant experience
C. Emotion because the speaker creates sadness
D. No appeal because it is short

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which feedback is most academically precise?

answer.text: C. The transition between reasons needs to be clearer.

feedback.text: Correct. This identifies the exact communication issue.
This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response gives clear instructional support?

feedback.text: Length is not the same as mastery.

answer.text: D. First identify the audience, then explain why tone matters.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response is a respectful disagreement?

answer.text: B. I understand your idea, but I think a calmer tone fits the audience better.

feedback.text: Correct. It acknowledges the idea and gives a reason.

answer.text: C. My idea is the only good one.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Why does audience matter when choosing tone?

answer.text: A. Every audience needs the same tone.

feedback.text: Tone affects how listeners receive a message.

answer.text: D. Tone should fit who is listening and why the message matters.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Speech excerpt: "Imagine a classroom where everyone feels heard before decisions are made." Which appeal is strongest?

answer.text: A. Emotion because the speaker creates a feeling of belonging

feedback.text: Correct. The image helps the audience feel the value of being heard.

answer.text: B. Trust because a role is named

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: C. Logic because there is a statistic
D. No appeal because it describes a classroom

feedback.text: The description is meant to affect the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

A speaker says, "The claim should come before the evidence." Which paraphrase is best?

answer.text: A. You think evidence should never appear.
B. You want only evidence and no claim.
C. You are saying the main idea should be stated before the support.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the meaning in new words.

answer.text: D. You do not care about order.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which academic word names the people receiving the message?

feedback.text: Correct. Audience means the listeners or viewers receiving the message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best clarifies a speaker's meaning?

answer.text: A. When you say stronger opening, do you mean more serious or more emotional?

feedback.text: Correct. This asks a specific clarifying question.
This states confusion without asking a useful question.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence best explains a communication choice?

answer.text: A. It is good because it is good.

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: D. The opening question helps the audience focus on the main claim.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains the choice with precise vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Which explanation best connects rhetoric to purpose?

answer.text: A. The speaker uses words because speeches need words.
B. The speaker uses evidence to persuade the audience that the plan will work.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the choice and connects it to purpose.
This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.
This does not explain a rhetorical choice.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which tone is least appropriate for group feedback?

feedback.text: Correct. Feedback should help improvement, not attack the speaker.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which question best asks for clarification?

feedback.text: This expresses frustration but does not ask a specific question.

answer.text: B. Can someone do this for me?
D. Could you clarify whether the response should be spoken or written?

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best shows active listening?

answer.text: A. I disagree before hearing the full point.
C. You are saying the audience needs a clearer example first.

feedback.text: This attacks the idea instead of listening.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Speech excerpt: "If each group uses a timer, speakers can keep their presentations within the limit." Which appeal is strongest?

answer.text: A. Emotion because the speaker describes fear
B. Logic because the speaker explains cause and effect

feedback.text: Correct. Using a timer leads to staying within the limit.

answer.text: C. No rhetoric because timers are tools

feedback.text: The speaker uses reasoning about the tool.

answer.text: D. Trust because the speaker gives credentials

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence is the clearest academic feedback?

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: D. Your conclusion restates the claim and reminds the audience of the purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. It identifies the speech part and its function.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q26

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which phrase best describes voice in communication?

answer.text: A. The speaker's style or presence in the message

feedback.text: Correct. Voice includes how the speaker comes across.

answer.text: B. Only how loud a speaker talks
C. The number of words in the speech

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q27

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response helps a peer understand the next step?

answer.text: B. First write your claim, then add one reason that supports it.
C. You missed the directions, so too bad.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q28

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which option is not a paraphrase?

answer.text: A. You think the evidence should come after the claim.
B. You are saying the audience needs a definition first.
C. You are wrong and should stop talking.

feedback.text: Correct. This is a judgment, not a paraphrase.

answer.text: D. You mean the tone should be more serious.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q29

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Which appeal focuses on speaker credibility?

feedback.text: Correct. Trust is connected to credibility and reliability.
Confusion is not a useful rhetorical appeal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q30

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response best supports collaboration?

answer.text: C. Let's compare both ideas and choose the one that fits our audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q31

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which tone best fits a speech encouraging students to join a cleanup project?

Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q32

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which revision replaces vague language with academic language?

answer.text: B. Add evidence after the claim so the audience understands your reason.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses precise academic language and explains the improvement.
This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q33

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

Speech excerpt: "Every student deserves to feel welcome in discussion." Which appeal is strongest?

answer.text: A. Logic because the speaker gives a number
B. Emotion because the speaker focuses on belonging

feedback.text: Correct. The statement appeals to fairness and feeling welcome.

answer.text: C. Trust because the speaker names a job

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: D. No appeal because it is about students

feedback.text: The statement is meant to affect how the audience feels.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q34

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best explains a submission expectation?

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.
This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: C. Submit one paragraph that explains your audience, tone, and reason.

feedback.text: Correct. This clearly states what to submit.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q35

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response shows listening before building?

answer.text: A. You are saying the audience needs an example; we could use a school scenario.

feedback.text: Correct. This paraphrases first and then builds.

answer.text: C. I did not hear you, but I have an idea.
D. I will change the topic now.

feedback.text: This does not build on the idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q36

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which vocabulary word means the reason for communicating?

feedback.text: Correct. Purpose is the reason for communicating.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q37

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.06

What should a complete rhetorical explanation include?

answer.text: A. A personal opinion with no evidence
C. The appeal, evidence from the excerpt, and how it supports purpose

feedback.text: Correct. This makes the explanation complete and text-based.
Details should connect to the rhetorical choice.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q38

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which message is most appropriate for a principal?

answer.text: B. Good morning. May I ask a question about the presentation schedule?

feedback.text: Correct. This is respectful, clear, and appropriate for the audience.

answer.text: D. You should already know what I want.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q39

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence uses the clearest academic language?

feedback.text: This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.
This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.
This answer does not fully meet the lesson standard. Recheck the audience, purpose, evidence, or communication skill before choosing.

answer.text: D. The introduction previews the main claim and prepares the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_Assessment_Q40

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which statement best summarizes Unit 1?

answer.text: A. Effective communication combines audience awareness, listening, tone, academic language, and rhetorical choices.

feedback.text: Correct. This summarizes the major Unit 1 skills.

answer.text: D. Communication is only about speaking louder.

feedback.text: Communication includes listening, audience, tone, language, and rhetoric.
